h1: The 5 Best Self-Propelled Garden Carts of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five electric self-propelled garden carts with loads from 440 to 660 lb, compared on battery, braking, folding and price tier.
summary: The SuperHandy 48V power wagon is our top pick for heavy-duty powered hauling. The VEVOR 36V cart adds a named brake and the same 660 lb load for less, the Landworks 500 lb cart is a simpler powered option, and the Litheli folds away when you are done. The BougeRV is the cheapest way to try powered hauling.
intro: A powered cart changes the job from pushing weight to steering it, which is a big deal on a sloped yard or for anyone with a bad back. The catch is that the battery, not the bed, decides how long the cart is useful, and listings rarely lead with runtime.

We reviewed five electric carts and left out the hand-pulled wagons that sometimes appear in the same search results. Ranking is based on the spec sheet: rated load, battery size, braking, folding design and price tier. None of these figures are measured by us, so treat them as manufacturer claims.

products.name: SuperHandy Utility Service Cart Power Wagon Wheelbarrow Electric 48V DC Li-Ion Powered, 660Lbs Load and 1000Lbs+ Hauling
products.verdict: The strongest powered hauler on the list, with a 48V lithium system.
products.description:
The SuperHandy runs on a 48V DC lithium-ion system and lists a 660 lb load with hauling beyond 1000 lb. That towing-level figure is higher than any other powered cart here.

It outranks the VEVOR because of the higher voltage and the larger pulling claim, though the VEVOR matches the 660 lb carrying number and lists a brake by name.

Buy it for farms and large properties. The caveat is the $500+ price tier and the weight that comes with a 48V battery.
products.idealFor: Large properties with regular heavy hauling.

products.name: VEVOR Electric Utility Cart, 36V 432Wh Battery Powered Electric Wagon, 500W Power Wheelbarrow with Brake, 660 lbs Load
products.verdict: Same carrying number as the leader, with a named brake and a stated battery size.
products.description:
This VEVOR uses a 36V, 432Wh battery with a 500W motor and a brake, and lists a 660 lb load. It is one of the few here that publishes watt-hours.

It ranks under the SuperHandy because it uses a lower-voltage system and has no stated hauling rating above the load figure. It is easier to judge, though, since the energy number is disclosed.

Suits hilly yards where a brake matters. The caveat is that $500+ is still a serious spend.
products.idealFor: Hilly yards where stopping control matters.

products.name: Landworks Electric Utility Cart, 500 lb Load
products.verdict: A simple self-propelled cart with a 500 lb load.
products.description:
The Landworks is a self-propelled electric cart with a 500 lb load. The listing keeps details sparse, with no battery capacity or brake named.

It ranks below the VEVOR because that cart discloses more, and it carries 160 lb less. It sits in the $500+ bucket but is positioned as a cheaper step down from the top pick.

Best for owners who want powered hauling without a long spec sheet. The caveat is that you should ask the seller for battery and runtime details before ordering.
products.idealFor: Owners wanting powered hauling without frills.
products.skipIf: You need battery details up front.

products.name: Litheli Electric Utility Wagon Cart, 150L Capacity, 450 lbs Load, Foldable Heavy-Duty Design with All-Terrain Wheels, Variable Speed Drive
products.verdict: Folds flat and gives you a speed dial.
products.description:
The Litheli is a 150 liter electric wagon rated for 450 lb with a foldable design, all-terrain wheels and a variable speed drive. It sits in the $200-500 bucket, well below the premium picks.

It ranks below the Landworks on load, but folding saves garage space and variable speed gives finer control near flower beds.

Ideal for small to mid-size yards with limited storage. The caveat is the lower 450 lb rating.
products.idealFor: Small yards with limited storage space.

products.name: BougeRV Electric Utility Wagon with 133Wh Battery, Up to 440 lbs Load
products.verdict: A low-cost way to try powered hauling.
products.description:
The BougeRV wagon has a 133Wh battery and lists up to 440 lb of load, in the $200-500 bucket. The battery is much smaller than the VEVOR's 432Wh pack.

It ranks last because the 133Wh battery implies shorter working time, but it costs less and makes sense for light, short trips.

Buy it for occasional yard work. The caveat is the limited battery, so avoid long, loaded hauls.
products.idealFor: Occasional light hauling on a budget.

whatMatters.detail: Watt-hours measure stored energy, so a 432Wh pack holds more than three times the energy of a 133Wh pack. More energy means longer work between charges. Look for Wh in the title or specs, not only voltage.
Load is what the bed carries, while hauling is a pulling claim that may include towing. A 660 lb load is plenty for most yards. Check which figure is the real carrying limit.
A powered cart can run away downhill with a full bed. A named brake or motor braking helps you hold position on slopes. Check the feature list for the word brake.
Variable speed lets you creep near plants and go faster on open ground. Fixed speed is simpler but less precise. Look for a dial or trigger described in the listing.
A folding wagon saves garage space but adds hinges that can loosen. If space is tight, it can be the deciding factor. Check for folded dimensions on the listing.

faq.q: Do self-propelled carts work on slopes?
faq.a: Yes, but a brake matters more than motor power. The VEVOR names a brake, so it is easier to trust on a hill with a full bed.
Buying on load rating alone. A cart with a large load and a small battery will run out of charge sooner than one with a smaller rating and a bigger pack.

faq.q: Is a powered cart worth it over a hand cart?
faq.a: If your yard is large, sloped, or you have back trouble, yes. For flat, short trips a cheaper hand-pulled cart is enough.
Use the supplied charger and follow the listing's guidance. Charge indoors, away from extreme heat or cold.

faq.q: How should I maintain the battery?
faq.a: Avoid leaving lithium packs fully drained for months. Store at a partial charge in a dry place.
Not advisable. Rain and temperature swings shorten battery life, so keep it under cover.

finalTake: The SuperHandy 48V wagon is the best self-propelled cart for people who actually need heavy hauling. The VEVOR is the smart buy for hills thanks to its brake and disclosed battery, the Landworks suits simple needs, and the Litheli wins on storage. If you only want to try powered hauling, the BougeRV is the lowest-risk start.
